### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A02 was not observed at all (0 of 200 traces); in the later window it occurs exactly once in every trace (participation 100%, mean 1.0 per trace, never repeated), always at the same final position in the trace. [OCC001, POS001]
- In the earlier window, A06 sat at the end of the trace (median normalized position 1.0 in all 200 traces); in the later window it appears earlier, at about 0.8 of the trace (median 0.8). [POS002]
- The relationship between the two activities changed completely: earlier, 100 in 100 traces contained A06 without A02; later, 100 in 100 traces contain both, always with A06 executed before A02. [REL001]
- A06's observed successor changed: in the earlier window only 4 outgoing transitions of A06 were seen (all to A04, consistent with A06 usually being the final step with no successor); in the later window all 200 observed outgoing transitions of A06 lead to A02. [DIR005]
- Minor shifts likely within sampling variation: from A03, the share to A06 fell from about 41% to 32% while A05 rose from 37% to 41% and A04 from 22% to 27%; from A04, the share to A06 rose from about 11% to 16%; A05's participation rose slightly from about 50 to 53 in 100 traces. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that in the later window A02 was added as a new, mandatory final step executed once after A06: A02 went from not observed (0 of 200 traces) to occurring exactly once in all 200 traces at a fixed end position, while A06 — previously the last step, with no observed successor in roughly 196 of 200 traces — now precedes A02 in every trace and is directly followed by it in all observed cases, which also accounts for A06's shift from the trace end (median 1.0) to about 0.8. [OCC001, POS001, POS002, REL001, DIR005]

The supporting signs are that occurrence, position, relation and successor indicators all reach the maximum empirical strength (about 0.995, i.e. differences larger than in all 200 random re-splits) and tell one coherent story; however, these items overlap and are not independent confirmations, the before-window successor profile of A06 rests on only 4 observations, and no chance-expectation baseline was provided to compare the number of items against. [OCC001, POS001, POS002, REL001, DIR005]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A02 occurred at a very low rate in the earlier window, since zero participation strictly means only that it was not observed there; likewise, the rare A06→A04 transition seen 4 times before cannot be characterised further. [OCC001, REL001, DIR005]

Other differences: small redistributions of outgoing shares at A01, A03, A04 and A05 (at most about 9 percentage points) and a slight rise in A05's participation, all of moderate strength (about 0.44–0.83) and consistent with sampling variation between two 200-trace windows. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, OCC002]
